reference.title: Scenario 2 — Admonition in a table cell
reference.shortdesc: Consider a table where one of the cells contains a Note or Warning paragraph styled

section.p: Consider a table where one of the cells contains a Note or Warning paragraph styled with an admonition style, rather than a plain Normal paragraph. This typically occurs when an author wants to call out a restriction or alert the reader about a specific table entry.

row.entry: [Table] — cell 1: Normal text / [Warning style]: Do not modify this value in production.

entry.codeblock:
Description

Normal text

Do not modify this value in production.

section.p: Result: When an admonition style is applied inside a table cell, the admonition adopts the context of the table structure. The converter wraps the content in a <note> element and places it inside the <stentry> or <entry> of the converted DITA table. The admonition is contained within the cell and rendered as an inline note within that cell's content. Because the admonition is contained in a table cell, it inherits the table's structural style and is treated as cell-level content rather than body-level content.
